chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about Al-Mubarat, how is it? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It happens that there is something for the woman upon her husband, from a dower or from something else, and it happens that he has given her part of it. So each one of them dislikes it (the marriage tie). So the woman says to her husband:

key_terms.أُبَارِئُكَ: I disavow/release you (from the remaining debt)
key_terms.الْمُبَارَاة: Al-Mubarat, a form of divorce by payment of debt/dower

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal procedure for Al-Mubarat divorce and how does the wife's payment affect the marital bond?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the mechanics of Al-Mubarat, a consensual divorce where the wife disavows her remaining dower or debt to the husband in exchange for immediate release. It highlights the reciprocal nature of this agreement, noting that the husband’s right to marital relations is contingent upon the wife’s finality in her declaration, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on mutual consent and financial settlement in dissolving the marriage bond.
